title: Grateful Dead Live at Metropolitan Sports Center on 1973-10-23
lineage: Dat (Sony D8) -> VXPocket v2 -> Samplitude Professional v10.1 -> FLAC (2 Discs Audio / 2 Discs FLAC)

ai_review.summary: Lovely soundboard capture with Keith's front‑mix organ and a stellar second set featuring Truckin', Let It Grow, The Other One and an unforgettable (though interrupted) Casey Jones.
ai_review.review: The recording is a well‑balanced soundboard mix – Keith’s organ sits up front, Bobby and Billy are a touch high but add excitement, and the early level tweaks settle after the first few tunes. Musically the show shines with a powerful second set (Truckin', Let It Grow, The Other One, Weather Report Suite) and memorable jams, though the third set was cut short by an on‑stage fight that left Casey Jones feeling tense.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating is 4.48/5 across 25 detailed comments; the show is praised for performance and the soundboard mix is consistently described as good to excellent.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, lovely sounding board with Keith's organ unusually forward. First few tunes have level‑adjustment issues; Bobby and Billy sit a bit high in the mix but add energy rather than detract.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong first two sets with creative jams and a unique sound‑check organ jam; third set was abruptly halted after an audience fight, leaving the band visibly upset but overall performance remains high.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Leads are extra‑inspired (especially on Truckin' and Let It Grow); sits back during parts of LIG allowing Keith to shine.
band_member_comments.Phil: Gets visibly upset during Casey Jones after the audience fight; otherwise provides solid, driving bass throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Pumped up on Mexicali Blues; his vocals/guitar are a bit high in the mix but add excitement.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's organ/electric piano is unusually forward, dominates the Wang Dang Doodle soundcheck jam and delivers a standout solo on Let It Grow.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming shines in the Drums segment; he even jumped offstage to help break up the fight.
